text.p: These are the leading stories in the Tunisian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali and his French counterpart Jaques Chirac had a telephone conversation on Thursday evening during which they expressed their attachment to boosting friendship and cooperation between the two countries.
- Ben Ali on Thursday chaired a cabinet meeting on exports. The High Export Council is to hold its first meeting soon.
- A consumption survey shows that people living in cities spend double what those living in rural areas do.
- Tunisia discusses with Sweden recycling debt in environment projects.
- Volvo Truck Corporation to assemble more truck models for the Tunisian market.
- Seven Tunisian associations protest against a meeting held in the Europen Parliament in Strasbourg on Tunisia's human rights record. Say the meeting was "neo-colonialist".
- A United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) report on Human Development 97 ranks Tunisia among the 14 countries which cut poverty by half.

- In free opinion column signed Fethi Mabrouk: former MP Khemais Chammari behaved as a traitor to his country by attending a European Parliament meeting on Tunisia's human rights record in Strasbourg this week.
- The European Investment Bank confirms its readiness to boost financial support to Tunisia.
